1.why: `ownedRecovery()` requires `recovery.sessionId === session.id` and the submitted token is hashed and compared only against that session's own recovery record.

2.why: A token is only valid against the tokenHash of the recovery owned by the requesting session, so another session's token is rejected — the statement is false.

3.why: There is no session rotation or invalidation after `/api/reset-password`; the same `sid` cookie/session object remains valid and continues to the next stages.

4.why: `Bun.serve` is configured with TLS cert/key (server refuses to start without them) and HSTS is set, but no explicit minimum/latest TLS version is pinned — it relies on Bun defaults.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes (and cleared after use) and passwords hashed with bcrypt cost 12, though the token itself is returned in plaintext as `mockToken`.

6.why: No email is ever generated; instead the recovery token is returned in the API response, printed into the page as `<code>` and logged to the on-page log and browser console, so no email-side guarding exists.

7.why: Email is length/regex validated, tokens and cookie values are checked with strict `^[a-f0-9]{64}$` patterns, body size is capped at 4096 bytes, and passwords are policy-checked, though the email validation result is discarded (`void validEmail`).

8.why: Navigation uses only same-origin hash routes from an allowlist (`recover|verify|mfa|reset|privacy|confirmation`), CSP sets `form-action 'self'` and `base-uri 'none'`, and no user-controlled redirect target exists.

9.why: There are no email templates at all in the code; the equivalent rendered content is built exclusively with `textContent`/`createElement` so no user HTML or script can be injected.

10.why: The client explicitly logs the reset token (`"Test reset token: " + state.mockToken`) and the MFA code to the visible log panel and console, even though server errors are generic.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and never stored plaintext, but the MFA secret is hardcoded in source as `const MFA_CODE = "246810"` and echoed to the UI.

12.why: The hardcoded, deterministic MFA code `246810` functions as a built-in default credential that always passes the second factor for every recovery.

13.why: Per-recovery attempt counters (`ATTEMPT_LIMIT = 5`) with 60s blocks plus per-IP sliding-window limits (`CLIENT_ATTEMPT_LIMIT`, `CLIENT_RECOVERY_LIMIT`) throttle token, MFA, and password attempts.

14.why: `/api/recovery` always returns the same generic "If an eligible account is available…" message and creates a recovery regardless of the supplied address, with the validity check deliberately discarded.

15.why: Tokens come from `randomHex(32)` using `crypto.getRandomValues` (256-bit), are single-use, expire in 15 minutes, and are bound to the specific session/recovery record.
